stories.headline: GSTR-7 for October 2026: GST TDS return due 10 November
points: Per the guide, GSTR-7 for October 2026 is due 10 November 2026 unless a later notification changes it.
Section 51 requires notified deductors to deduct 2% GST TDS when a contract's taxable value exceeds ₹2.5 lakh.
The guide says GST TDS reaches the deductee's cash ledger and is not input tax credit, so it needs separate reconciliation.
stories.why_it_matters: GST TDS rules, tax-head choice and reconciliation of deductions are core compliance topics for CA and CMA students working in GST.
stories.source_title: Goods and Services Tax | GSTR-7 for October 2026: GST TDS Return, Deductee Credit and Reconciliation Controls
check_notes: Point 2 presents 2% as a flat rule. The source calls it the 'standard' 2% in aggregate (1% CGST + 1% SGST/UTGST, or 2% IGST), subject to a place-of-supply exception where no deduction is made. It also says the ₹2.5 lakh threshold excludes GST and cess. Adding these qualifiers would make the point more precise.
The 'Why it matters' line about CA and CMA students is editorial framing that the source doesn't state. It's acceptable as context, not as a factual claim.

stories.headline: ITAT deletes ₹4.42 lakh penalty over late PF, ESI deposits
points: ITAT Ahmedabad removed a ₹4,42,866 Section 270A misreporting penalty on Nascent Info Technologies for AY 2017-18.
The officer had disallowed ₹7.16 lakh of employee PF and ESI contributions that were deposited after the due dates.
Tribunal held a disallowance alone is not misreporting; the department must show a case under Section 270A(9).
stories.why_it_matters: Shows the difference between a disallowance and a penalty under Section 270A, a key point in tax assessments and penalty work.
stories.source_title: PF contributions deposited late? Can the income tax department impose a penalty on your employer? ITAT clarifies

stories.headline: ITAT Cuttack deletes tax audit penalty for share trading loss case
points: ITAT Cuttack deleted a Section 271B penalty for AY 2013-14 against individual Ratan Kumar Kejriwal.
The assessee said his share losses were not business activity, so no audit was required.
Tribunal noted the Revenue's own scrutiny selection reason described him as having no business, and called this decisive.
stories.why_it_matters: Section 271B penalty depends on whether a business exists and an audit was required, a key point in tax audit and penalty work.
stories.source_title: Income Tax | Share Trading Loss Without Business Activity Does Not Justify Tax Audit Penalty: ITAT Cuttack
